'''Julius Melvin Hodge''' (born November 18, 1983) is an American and Antiguan<ref>{{cite web |title=Julius Melvin Hodge - Player Profile |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/player/163141/Julius-Melvin-Hodge |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=1 September 2024 |language=en}}</ref> [[basketball]] coach and former professional player who is the head coach for the [[Lincoln (Pennsylvania) Lions|Lincoln Lions men's basketball team]]. Originally from [[Harlem, New York]], Hodge played [[college basketball]] for the [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State Wolfpack]] and was selected 20th overall in the [[2005 NBA draft]] by the [[Denver Nuggets]]. The [[ACC Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]] during the 2003–04 season, Hodge finished his college career by leading State to the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|Sweet 16]].

==Early life==
Julius Hodge was born in the [[Manhattan]] neighborhood of Harlem and raised across the [[Harlem River]] from [[Yankee Stadium (1923)|Yankee Stadium]].<ref name=ackert>{{cite news|last1=Ackert|first1=Kristie|title=HARLEM'S HODGE LEADER OF PACK. His work isn't done at N.C. State|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/archives/sports/harlem-hodge-leader-pack-work-isn-n-state-article-1.567964|access-date=6 July 2015|work=[[New York Daily News]]|date=March 24, 2005}}</ref> His mother, Mary Hodge, worked two jobs, including as a [[Teaching assistant|teacher's aide]], to support Julius and his two siblings.<ref name=ackert /><ref name=paxinos>{{cite web|last1=Paxinos|first1=Stathi|date=November 12, 2009|title=New Tiger looks on lighter side|url=http://newsstore.fairfax.com.au/apps/viewDocument.ac;jsessionid=94FD5D03811E287EA654316407E34E13?sy=afr&pb=all_ffx&dt=selectRange&dr=1month&so=relevance&sf=text&sf=headline&rc=10&rm=200&sp=brs&cls=3362&clsPage=1&docID=AGE091112GA7C16SLL8I|website=[[The Australian Financial Review]]|publisher=[[Fairfax Media]]|access-date=6 July 2015}}</ref>

Hodge became smitten with basketball when he was five years old after his father took him to a [[New York Knicks]] game against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] at [[Madison Square Garden]] where [[Magic Johnson]] smiled at him in the crowd.<ref name=ackert /> Hodge's father was [[deported]] to [[Antigua and Barbuda]] when Hodge was nine years old and Hodge has not seen him since.<ref name=paxinos /> Hodge's older brother, Steven, was his strongest male role model and played basketball in the [[NJCAA]] at [[Sullivan County Community College]] and later in [[NCAA Division II]] at [[Stony Brook Southampton#Southampton College, Long Island University|Long Island University – Southampton]]. Steven made the decision to name his younger brother after all-time basketball great [[Julius Erving]].<ref name=collins>{{cite book|last1=Collins|first1=Dan|title=The ACC basketball book of fame|date=2013|publisher=John F. Blair|isbn=978-0-89587-606-5|page=43}}</ref>

==High school career==
As a senior at [[St. Raymond High School for Boys]], operated by the [[Institute of the Brothers of the Christian Schools|De La Salle Christian Brothers]], in [[the Bronx]], New York, Hodge was part of the 2001 [[McDonald's All-American Team]] and the [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|First-team ''Parade'' All-American]], [[New York Mr. Basketball Award|New York State Mr. Basketball]], ''[[New York Daily News]]'' Player of the Year, New York All-Metro Squad, and ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'''s [[Old Spice]] Athlete of the Month. He scored a total of 684 points his senior season, setting the school record at St. Raymond High School, and left rated as the best [[shooting guard]] by [[ESPN]] and fifth-best nationally. He averaged 24.5 points, 5 assists and 4 steals per game.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-2001-04-07-0104070246-story.html|title=STARGAZING IN THE CITY|newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Sakamoto, Bob|date=April 7, 2001|access-date=October 8, 2019}}</ref> Hodge surprised basketball fans by choosing to attend [[North Carolina State University]] over [[Syracuse University]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Pitoniak|first1=Scott|title=N.C. State's Hodge hopes for a happy N.Y. homecoming|url=http://roc.democratandchronicle.com/article/20050325/SPORTS0102/503250389/N-C-State-s-Hodge-hopes-happy-N-Y-homecoming|access-date=6 July 2015|work=[[Democrat and Chronicle]]|date=March 25, 2005}}</ref>

==College career==
{{more citations needed section|date=August 2024}}
As a freshman with the [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State Wolfpack]], he was the leading freshman scorer in the ACC, averaging 10.7 points per game. He was named to second-team All-ACC Tournament team, after averaging 12.3 points. He earned the [[Lorenzo Charles]] Offensive Rebounding Award for 2002, [[Dick Vitale]]'s "Diaper Dandy" and ranked 20th in the ACC in rebounding. He scored a double-double in his first collegiate game and his first ACC game. He was the only Pack player with multiple double-doubles for the 2001–2002 season.

For the 2002–03 campaign, Hodge was selected as a First Team All-ACC player. He recorded four career-highs during the three-day run to the finals of the [[2003 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]]. He recorded his seventh double-double during the final game of the tournament and ranked seventh in free throw percentage for the season. During this season he recorded the first-ever [[triple-double]] in Wolfpack history, and was named ACC Player of the Week after leading the Pack to back-to-back victories against [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]]. He was one of 17 finalists to make the U.S. squad for the [[2003 Pan American Games]] and Dick Vitale named Hodge to his "All-Rolls Royce Team." He was one of the 50 preseason candidates for the [[John R. Wooden Award|Wooden Award]].

During the [[2005 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2005 NCAA tournament]], Hodge hit a game winning shot against [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] after [[Charlie Villanueva]] had tied the score.

After concluding his senior season and entering the [[NBA draft]], Hodge remained at [[NC State]] to finish his degree in communications.<ref name=tbt />

==Professional career==
===NBA===
Hodge was chosen in the first round (20th overall) of the 2005 NBA Draft by the Denver Nuggets. He appeared in 14 games for the Nuggets in the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]] while averaging only 0.9 points in 2.4 minutes.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/julius_hodge/career_stats.html Julius Hodge playerfile: career stats] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203093924/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/julius_hodge/career_stats.html |date=2013-12-03 }}, ''nba.com''</ref>

On January 5, 2007, Hodge started in his first career NBA game, against the Los Angeles Lakers. Six days later he was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] along with [[Earl Boykins]] for [[Steve Blake]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2727760 ESPN – Nuggets deal Boykins, Hodge to Bucks for Blake – NBA<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> On February 7 of that year, Hodge was waived by the Bucks.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nba_news/20070208042744840000201_story.html NBA.com Bucks Waive Hodge, Recall Markota<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> Later that year, he played for the 2007 [[Seattle SuperSonics]] summer league team.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/sonics/news/recap070706.html SONICS: Durant, Green Welcomed to NBA in Summer Opener<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

===Italy===
On August 10, 2007, Hodge signed with [[Italy|Italian]] [[Serie A (basketball)|Serie A]] team [[Pallacanestro Varese|Cimberio Varese]]. Midway through the season, he transferred to fellow Serie A team [[Legea Scafati]].<ref>[http://it.eurosport.yahoo.com/20122007/8/scafati-via-romero-hodge-arriva-babrauskas.html Scafati: via Romero e Hodge, arriva Babrauskas – Yahoo! Eurosport IT<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> In Italy, Hodge had trouble getting his clubs to fulfill his salary obligations.<ref name=villagevoice>{{cite news|last1=Rayman|first1=Graham|title=JULIUS HODGE: HARLEM GLOBE-TROTTER|url=http://www.villagevoice.com/news/julius-hodge-harlem-globe-trotter-6392219|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150708010859/http://www.villagevoice.com/news/julius-hodge-harlem-globe-trotter-6392219|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 8, 2015|access-date=7 July 2015|work=[[Village Voice]]|date=November 24, 2009}}</ref>

===Adelaide 36ers===

====2007–08 season====
On December 21, 2007, Hodge signed with the [[Adelaide 36ers]] in the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|NBL]] as their second import to replace the outgoing [[Mike Chappell]]. He finished his contract with Italian Serie A team Legea Scafati and arrived in Adelaide on December 23 after making trips to his hometown New York. He made his debut for the 36ers against the [[South Dragons]] helping them to a victory.<ref name="adelaide36ers.com">[http://www.adelaide36ers.com/36ers/media/news/366/ Adelaide Pura Milk 36ers | Media – 36ers News | Pure Excitement<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080423073141/http://www.adelaide36ers.com/36ers/media/news/366/ |date=2008-04-23 }}</ref>
On January 29, Hodge was rewarded with the league's player of the week for round 19 after averaging 27 points, 4 rebounds and 4.5 assists in the two games the 36ers played, which included a dominant performance of 39 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists against the [[Cairns Taipans]].<ref>[http://nbl.com.au/default.aspx?s=newsdisplay&id=74066 NBL > News<!-- Bot generated title -->]{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
On February 2, Hodge became the first 36er since [[Robert Rose (basketball)|Robert Rose]] in 1994 to record a triple double (24 points, 12 rebounds, 13 assists). A few days after, on February 5, Hodge won his second and back-to-back player of the week for Round 20 after averaging 31 points, 10.5 rebounds and 9.5 assists, which also included a performance of 37 points, 9 rebounds, and 6 assists in the 36ers lost to the [[Gold Coast Blaze]].<ref>[http://nbl.com.au/default.aspx?s=newsdisplay&id=74166 NBL > News<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160405215148/http://www.nbl.com.au/default.aspx?s=newsdisplay&id=74166 |date=2016-04-05 }}</ref> On February 12, Hodge won his third consecutive player of the week for round 21 by having another dominant performance of 31 points, 14 rebounds and 9 assists in the 36ers win against the Cairns Taipans. Hodge became just the second player to win the award three times ([[Chris Anstey]] is the other player to do so), and the first player to win it three times consecutively during the season.<ref>[http://nbl.com.au/default.aspx?s=newsdisplay&id=74271 NBL > News<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160409172319/http://www.nbl.com.au/default.aspx?s=newsdisplay&id=74271 |date=2016-04-09 }}</ref> Despite only playing half of the season in the league, Hodge was rewarded with the [[NBL (Australia) All NBL teams|All NBL Third Team]] for his efforts with the 36ers. Hodge then bid for his return to the NBA by trying out with the [[New Jersey Nets]], but could not make the regular season roster despite signing a 2-year non-guaranteed contract.

====2008–09 season====
On November 15, 2008, Hodge re-signed with the Adelaide 36ers replacing outgoing import [[Mark Tyndale]].<ref>[http://www.adelaide36ers.com/36ers/media/news/467/ Adelaide Pura Milk 36ers  > Julius Hodge returns to 36ers<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090106140550/http://www.adelaide36ers.com/36ers/media/news/467/ |date=2009-01-06 }}</ref> In the first week of his return to the NBL, Hodge won another NBL Player of the Week award for round 10, averaging 26.5 points per game, 10.5 rebounds, 6 assists, and 1 steal, despite the 36ers losing the two games he played in.<ref>[http://nbl.com.au/default.aspx?s=newsdisplay&id=76771 NBL > News<!-- Bot generated title -->]{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> This included a dominant performance of 27 points, 8 rebounds, and 8 assists against the [[South Dragons]], and the praise of opposition coach [[Brian Goorjian]], who coached the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian Boomers]] in the [[2008 Beijing Olympics]], saying that he was "possibly the best player in the league."<ref>[http://nbl.com.au/default.aspx?s=matchreportdisplay&id=76759 NBL > News<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160414215813/http://www.nbl.com.au/default.aspx?s=matchreportdisplay&id=76759 |date=2016-04-14 }}</ref> On December 30, 2008, Hodge won his second NBL Player of the Week award of the season for round 15, after having scored 31 points (while shooting 13 of 19 from the field at a 68% clip) and pulling 8 rebounds to lead the 36ers in a crucial road victory over the [[Melbourne Tigers]].<ref>[http://nbl.com.au/default.aspx?s=newsdisplay&id=77057 NBL > News<!-- Bot generated title -->]{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

In 2011, it was revealed Hodge's recruitment had been paid for out of the $27 million Christopher Wayne Fuss had embezzled from [[Flinders University]].<ref>http://www.adelaidenow.com.au/news/south-australia/former-flinders-university-cashier-christopher-fuss-admits-26m-fraud/story-e6frea83-1226015883278 Former Flinders University cashier Christopher Fuss admits $27m fraud</ref> On July 8, 2011, Fuss received nine years jail for the theft.<ref>http://www.abc.net.au/news/2011-07-08/man-jailed-for-stealing-27m-from-uni/2787234 Man jailed for stealing $27m from uni</ref>

===Melbourne Tigers===
In the summer of 2009, Hodge attended a [[Chicago Bulls]] mini-camp but did not make the team's roster.<ref name=villagevoice /> In November 2009, Hodge signed with the [[Melbourne Tigers]] to help bolster an injury-plagued roster missing [[Chris Anstey]].<ref>Hodge signs with Tigers [http://www.news.com.au/adelaidenow/story/0,22606,26322964-12428,00.html Ex-Sixer Julius Hodge joins Melbourne]</ref>  In his November 14, 2009 debut, Hodge scored 22 points and tallied 9 rebounds and 7 assists, but it wasn't enough as the [[Townsville Crocodiles]] won 98–91.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.fibalivestats.com/matches/1329/01/04/68/21n6uvgEF3bjc/ |title=FIBA LiveStats |access-date=2009-11-22 |archive-date=2016-03-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303220905/http://www.fibalivestats.com/matches/1329/01/04/68/21n6uvgEF3bjc/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Hodge returned to Adelaide as a member of the Melbourne Tigers in December 2009. He was booed every time he touched the ball and after the win Hodge stamped on [[Brett Maher (basketball)|Brett Maher]]'s signature on center court.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zbDos4P9A5o Hodge disrespects the 36ers and stomps on logo]</ref> He had to receive a police escort off the court and out of the building.

===Trotamundos de Carabobo===
Hodge returned to the Americas in 2010 after signing a contract with [[Trotamundos de Carabobo]] of Venezuela's [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Carchia|first1=E.|date=April 5, 2010|title=Trotamundos tab Hodge and Brown|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/81171/trotamundos-tab-hodge-and-brown.html|website=Sportando|access-date=7 July 2015}}</ref>

===Guangzhou Free Man===
After a brief stint in Venezuela, Hodge was signed in the summer of 2010 by [[Guangzhou]] Free Man of China's [[National Basketball League (China)|National Basketball League]]. He scored 16 points in his debut against [[Shenyang]].<ref name="free man sign">{{cite web|title=Guangzhou Free Man sign Julius Hodge|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/China/basketball.aspx?NewsID=196913|website=Asia-basket|publisher=Eurobasket|access-date=7 July 2015}}</ref>

===Petrochimi Bandar Imam===
Later in 2010, Hodge received a substantial offer from [[Petrochimi Bandar Imam BC]] of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League]]. Although impressed by the quality of basketball in Iran, Hodge was not comfortable with the environment. On March 3, 2011, Hodge and the club agreed to terminate his contract because they were unable to pay him the full amount.

===Tsmoki-Minsk===
Hodge's first new team of 2011 was [[BC Tsmoki-Minsk]], a [[Belarusian Premier League (basketball)|Belarusian Premier League]] team in [[Minsk]]. Due to a struggling economy, the club was slow to make payments and Hodge ultimately exercised an option to exit his contract early.<ref name=tbt />

===Jiangsu Tongxi===
Hodge returned to China in 2011, this time playing for the [[Jiangsu Monkey King|Jiangsu Tongxi]]. In seven games with Jiangsu, he averaged 25.6 points per game and was named the All-Chinese NBL Import Player of the Year.<ref name=newcomer>{{cite web|date=November 21, 2012|title=Julius Hodge is a newcomer at Paris-Levallois|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/news_print.asp?NewsID=296238|website=Eurobasket|access-date=7 July 2015}}</ref>

===Saigon Heat===
In December 2011, Hodge signed with [[Vietnam]]'s [[SSA Saigon Heat|Saigon Heat]] of the [[ASEAN Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lookatvietnam.com/2011/12/saigon-heat-sets-high-target-for-first-tourney.html |title=Saigon Heat sets high target for first tourney | Look at Vietnam |website=www.lookatvietnam.com |access-date=22 May 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120908102608/http://www.lookatvietnam.com/2011/12/saigon-heat-sets-high-target-for-first-tourney.html |archive-date=8 September 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
On February 20, 2012, the Heat released him.<ref>[http://www.aseanbasketballleague.com/news/detail/6880/saigon-heat-releases-julius-hodge Saigon Heat Releases Julius Hodge]</ref> Hodge described playing in Vietnam as an "adventure" where he had the unique experience of playing alongside teammates who worked [[Job (role)#Day job|9–5 jobs]].<ref name=tbt />

===Paris-Levallois===
In November 2012, Hodge was added to the roster of [[Paris-Levallois Basket]] in France's [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>[http://www.parislevallois.com/offres/gestion/actus_549_15281-685/have-you-met-julius.html Have You Met Julius?]</ref> In Paris, he was teammates with [[Sean May]] and [[Jawad Williams]], both of whom were Hodge's conference rivals in college and his teenage friends from the youth basketball circuit.<ref name=tbt />

===Saint John Mill Rats===
The [[Saint John Mill Rats]] of the [[National Basketball League of Canada]] announced the signing of Hodge on February 4, 2013. Hodge became just the ninth former NBA player to ever play in the league.<ref>{{cite web|date=February 4, 2013|title=Julius Hodge Taking His Talents to Mispec Beach|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4542596|website=OurSports Central|access-date=7 July 2015}}</ref> The club bought out his contract with Paris-Levallois Basket later that month on February 25.<ref>{{cite web|title=NBL Canada Transactions in 2012 – 2013 Season|url=http://www.nblcanada.com/14551/transactions-archive|publisher=[[National Basketball League of Canada]]|access-date=7 July 2015}}</ref>

==National team==
In 2011, Hodge played for the [[Antigua and Barbuda national basketball team]] in the [[FIBA CBC Championship|Caribbean Basketball Confederation Championship]].<ref>{{cite web |date=July 24, 2011|title=Day One in Nassau|url= https://www.latinbasket.com/FIBA-Caribbean-Championship/news/234781/Day-One-in-Nassau |website=[[latinbasket.com]]|access-date=August 31, 2024}}</ref>

==Post-playing career==
On May 18, 2015, [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|Buffalo Bulls]] head coach [[Nate Oats]] announced that Hodge would serve as the Director of Player Development for the [[State University of New York at Buffalo]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Julius Hodge Named Director of Player Development|url=http://www.ubbulls.com/sports/mbkb/2014-15/releases/20150518ewitkx|website=UBBulls.com|publisher=[[Buffalo Bulls|University at Buffalo Athletics]]|access-date=6 July 2015|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304023947/http://www.ubbulls.com/sports/mbkb/2014-15/releases/20150518ewitkx|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On March 29, 2016, Hodge joined his former college coach [[Herb Sendek]] as an assistant coach at [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara University]].<ref>[https://www.ubbullrun.com/buffalo-basketball/2016/3/29/11320826/julius-hodge-to-join-herb-sendek-santa-clara-broncos Julius Hodge to join Herb Sendek as assistant coach for Santa Clara Broncos]</ref>

On April 26, 2018, Hodge joined the staff of [[Jean Prioleau]] at [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Jose State]] as an assistant coach.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sjsuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062618aad.html|title=Julius Hodge Named San Jose State Men's Basketball Assistant Coach|publisher=San Jose State University|work=SJSUSpartans.com|access-date=June 26, 2018|date=June 26, 2018|archive-date=September 2, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180902123030/http://www.sjsuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062618aad.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In July 2021, Hodge became an assistant coach at [[Little Rock Trojans men's basketball|Little Rock]].

==Personal life==
After visiting a nightclub on April 8, 2006, Hodge was on [[Interstate 76 (west)|Interstate 76]] in North [[Denver]] around 2:00 a.m. when another vehicle pulled alongside his and fired several shots. Hodge was told he came within 5 minutes of bleeding to death. The case has yet to be solved.<ref name="espn_shooting">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2401667|title=Nuggets' Hodge shot and wounded on highway|date=April 8, 2006|agency=Associated Press|work=[[ESPN]]|access-date=13 March 2010}}</ref>

During each offseason of his overseas playing career, Hodge returned to live in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]] where he played during his college career. As of 2013, Hodge is married with two children. He describes himself as a "movie buff."<ref name=tbt>{{cite web|date=June 13, 2013|title=Throwback Thursday: Julius Hodge|url=http://www.gopack.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/061313aaa.html|website=NC State University Official Athletic Site|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=6 July 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150706174208/http://www.gopack.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/061313aaa.html|archive-date=6 July 2015}}</ref>
